facts.text: High-Gain Antenna was deployed at Chryse Planitia during Viking 1 in 1976.

The S-band high-gain antenna transmitted data directly to Earth at up to 16 kilobits per second. It also relayed data through the Viking Orbiter. The dish antenna is one of the most recognisable features of the Viking lander design.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Enabled the first direct data relay from the Martian surface to Earth at up to 16 kilobits per second, transmitting images and science data.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Chryse Planitia.
The antenna's relay architecture became the template for every subsequent Mars surface mission's communication design.
